LESSON: READING 12.2. 1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we enjoy reading poems?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication
2. apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression
3. respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 12.2. 1 INTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 12.2. 1 INTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression

What this means
In this part you learn to apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading to a partner. (skill: apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication.
3. Practise this skill: apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression.
4. Practise this skill: respond to questions based on a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for comprehension.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we enjoy reading poems?
2. How are poems different from stories?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 12.2. 1 Intensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a poem, song or passage containing proverbs with expression for effective communication.
5. Be able to: apply basic stress and rhythm when reading a poem, song or passage containing proverbs for self-expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
